newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ANALYSTS' COMMENTS ON VNU 1996 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS' COMMENTS ON VNU 1996 RESULTS.

text.p: Dutch publisher NV Verenigd Bezit VNU on Tuesday reported a 16 percent rise in net profit from ordinary operations to 316 million guilders in 1996.
The results were in line with analysts expectations of a net profit from ordinary operations of 312-317 million guilders.
Below is a collection of analysts comments on the results:

"When you look at the breakdown of operating profit, the sharp increse in consumer magazines is expected. What is very positive is that business-to-business publishing has become more important for VNU.

"This is highlighted by the increase in operating profit of 43 percent in Europe and 46 percent in the United States. I regard that as very positive because the mix of sales is increasingly shifting to business-to-business."

"Turnover growth somewhat lagged my expectations. That was due to the decreasing growth at newspapers and consumer magazines in the second half of 1996. The margin development was good in all activities. Profit growth was driven by business information activities, as expected."

"My first reaction is that I am very positive about the result and its quality. Magazines especially were very good. Margins improved from 13.5 percent to 15.1 percent. That's a terrific step in the right direction. Newspapers are quite a different story. (Their) results are a bit disappointing but there are a lot of costs taken into the result for the start of regional TV. We don't know how much. Business information is a very good result. Margins improved further, especially in the U.S., from 13.8 percent to 17.7 percent. Organic growth of nine percent in the underlying business is very good."
